### Observed differences

- The execution order between two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A26 and A27 each ran before A35, A36 and A41 in about 98–99 in 100 traces; in the later window, A35, A36 and A41 each run before A26 and A27 in about 97–98 in 100 traces. All these activities still occur together in every trace in both windows, so participation did not change — only the order did. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- Event positions moved accordingly: in the later window A35, A36 and A41 sit at about 42% of the trace, down from about 58–59% earlier, while A27 moved from about 38% to about 47% and A26 from about 53% to about 62%. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Direct successors were rerouted on both sides. In the earlier window A25 led to A27 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A26 led to A41, A35 or A36; in the later window A25 leads to A36, A41 or A35 (roughly one third each) and A26 leads to A30 in about 98 in 100. A35, A36 and A41, which earlier exited to A30 in about 28–34 in 100 of their transitions, now exit to A27 in about 31–33 in 100. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Step distances match this rerouting. In the later window A25 reaches A35 and A35 reaches A27 within one to four steps, each in about 199 of 200 traces (earlier: 1 trace each), and A26 reaches A30 in one step in about 99 in 100 traces (earlier: four to five steps). The earlier short paths — A25 to A27 in one step, A26 to A35/A36/A41 and A35/A36/A41 to A30 within one to three steps — survive in only 1–2 traces each. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block formed by A35, A36 and A41 and the segment formed by A27 and A26 reversed their execution order, with A25 and A30 rewired around them. In the earlier window the flow ran A25 → A27, then A26 fed the block A35/A36/A41, which exited to A30; in the later window A25 feeds the block, the block exits to A27, and A26 connects directly to A30, so the block now runs before A27 and A26 while A30 follows A26 instead of the block. The internal transitions among A35, A36 and A41 are unchanged. Supporting signs: the reversal is near-deterministic in both directions with 100% co-occurrence, so participation and repetition are unchanged; the successor changes show the rerouting directly; positions and step distances agree in direction and size; every item's difference exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits; and 26 qualifying items against roughly 0.63 expected without change makes chance an implausible explanation of the pattern as a whole. Limitations: the six relation items are pairwise views of one reversal and the position, distance and direction items largely re-describe the same swap, so they are not independent confirmations; the after-profiles of the vanished adjacencies rest on only 1–2 traces; and the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering applied to all traces from a shift in the mix of two stable order-variants between the windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG007]

Other differences: a few rare successors appear in the later window at about 1 in 200 rates (for example from A25 to A04/A14/A21/A33/A38/A45, from A36 to A02/A08/A19/A48 and from A41 to A02/A04/A08/A44/A45); at these rates they are consistent with sampling noise rather than a structural addition. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
